issue: Q's normative arkoor-cosign validation list says "Q also verifies: the per-vTXO seq strictly increments". No per-vTXO sequence exists in v0.3: per ERRATA/A6/A7 and event-kinds §3.10, seq is the global per-cosign-batch transfer-log sequence, and the nullifier is outpoint-only. "Per-vTXO seq" is a surviving v0.2 artifact of the H(outpoint‖seq) design and contradicts the companion spec.
suggestion: Replace with "the transfer-log seq strictly increments (one root per cosign batch, §3.10 of event-kinds.md)" or delete the clause, since the nullifier-absence check already covers double-cosign detection.

issue: Says "because the v0.3 review showed the v0.2 claim 'Q must unroll to sweep' was simply false". The review was of the v0.2 drafts (research/raw/review-v0.2-findings.json); the whitepaper itself elsewhere calls it "the v0.2 review" (§8.3 table, lines 375–380) and "a 51-finding verification review of the v0.2 drafts".
suggestion: Change "the v0.3 review" to "the v0.2 review" for consistency with §8.3 and the artifact name.

issue: The summary table drifts from the normative table in analysis/comparison.md §1: "Infra dependency: Public Nostr relays only" omits the tower market and operator archival relays that A2/A8 made load-bearing (comparison.md says "Nostr relays (incl. operator archival) + tower market"); the "Operator trust" cell ("4-of-7 theft; uncheckpointed window only") omits the A3 sender-alone-vs-offline-receiver clause that comparison.md's cell includes.
suggestion: Align the two cells with comparison.md §1: add "(incl. operator archival) + tower market" to Infra dependency and the sender-alone caveat to Operator trust.

issue: Labels "0.8%/mo" as "(top of band)". The posted band is 0.5–0.9%/month, so the top is 0.9%; 0.8% is the break-even per §1.2 and ERRATA. Whitepaper §9 explicitly computes the top of band as 0.9% ("0.9% × 10 BTC = 0.09"), so the label is internally and cross-document inconsistent.
suggestion: Relabel as "0.8%/mo (≈break-even, near top of band)" or recompute the row at 0.9% and adjust the reconciliation text.

issue: Same headline example (10k users, 100k-sat average) is modeled with different assumptions: whitepaper §9 assumes all 10 BTC hot (float ≈19 BTC, revenue "0.2–0.3 BTC/month" counting 0.15 BTC pinning) while economics §1.3 assumes 5 BTC hot (float ≈10 BTC, margin "+1.2–1.7M sats/month split seven ways", pinning unmodeled). Both are self-consistent, but a reader gets two materially different viability pictures with no cross-reference to the divergent assumptions.
suggestion: Pick one hot-fraction assumption (or have whitepaper §9 explicitly note economics.md's 50%-hot variant and the pinning-revenue treatment difference) so the two reconciliations visibly agree.

issue: Heading states "(Alice → Bob, ~1–2 s)" without the A19-mandated qualifier. Amendment A19 requires marking the 1–2 s arkoor latency as a "target pending measurement over relay+Tor paths"; whitepaper (§1.3, §4.3, §7.1) and comparison.md carry the qualifier, ceremonies.md does not.
suggestion: Change to "~1–2 s target, pending measurement over relay+Tor paths" to match the other documents.

issue: The A12 intent bond is a pre-signed tx spending a 1,000-sat 'bond vTXO', but the protocol's own minimum leaf denomination is 10,000 sats and sub-floor value 'cannot occupy its own leaf' (onchain §2.5, economics §3) — a 1,000-sat bond vTXO cannot exist as specified. 'Immediately broadcastable' is also wrong on L1: the bond tx spends a leaf whose prevout exists only after an unroll, so collecting 1k sats costs Q ~1.6 kvB (~16k sats @10 sat/vB). No doc reconciles either point.
suggestion: Explicitly exempt bond vTXOs from the 10k floor (or make the bond a sub-output of a normal leaf with change), and specify the collection path — e.g., Q holds the signed bond tx as a lien valid on any future unroll and/or nets the bond at the next cosign/refresh — rather than claiming immediate broadcastability.

issue: The A5 stack-margin reconciliation diverges materially between the two docs for the same canonical 10k-user/100k-sat pool: whitepaper treats all 10 BTC as hot and counts pinning at full adoption (0.15 BTC/mo) as a hard line, concluding ~0.2–0.3 BTC/mo revenue vs ~0.08 cost (≈3.5× covered); economics models 50% hot, marks pinning/gateway 'unmodeled', and concludes a thin +1.2–1.7M sats/mo margin with the headline product 'sold at or below cost'.
suggestion: Align the two worked examples (same hot fraction, same turnover, same treatment of pinning adoption), or have §9 explicitly state it assumes full pinning adoption and 100% hot balances and cite economics §1.3 as the conservative case.

issue: States 'all of a round's cell txs confirm in the same window, so the round's cells share an effective T_exp', contradicting event-kinds §3.9, which mandates per-cell t_exp precisely because 'a rebuilt cell may confirm at a different height than its siblings... these fields are per-cell, never round-wide'. A leftover round-level simplification from the pre-A1 single-round-tx model.
suggestion: Replace with: T_exp is strictly per cell (cell-tx height + 4320); sibling cells usually confirm within a few blocks but a rebuilt cell may differ, per event-kinds §3.9.

issue: The '144–720 blocks depending on which hop attacks' response window is applied uniformly to both defense cases, but the 144 floor exists only in the forfeit case (a refresh-stale hop-4 attacker, nSeq 144, onchain §3.4). In the uncheckpointed-chain stale-owner case (T5/A3) the attacker is a prior owner at hop ≤3, so the earliest a stale claim matures is 288 blocks after unroll — the stated 144 lower bound corresponds to no ladder attack.
suggestion: Scope the bounds: 288–720 blocks for stale-owner ladder attacks on uncheckpointed chains; 144–720 for forfeit defense of refresh-stale leaves. Conservative as written, but the conflation muddies the tower-response requirement.

issue: Churn-attack leverage figures disagree with each other and with their own arithmetic: economics §1.1 says hourly refresh strands '~1,390 tranches' (58 days × 24, correct) but calls this 'capital leverage in the hundreds'; attacks G4 says 'order 100–250× leverage' for the same hourly-refresh attack under the same 58-day lock, where refreshes-in-the-lock-window is ~1,392.
suggestion: Use one figure: ~1,390× theoretical leverage for unthrottled hourly refresh, reduced to whatever the minimum-dwell-time and per-leaf rate limits actually permit (state that derived bound in G4).

issue: Refers to 'the v0.3 review showed the v0.2 claim ... was simply false', while every other reference (§4.2, §8.3, attacks.md preamble, economics §2.3) calls the same 51-finding event 'the v0.2 review' or 'the verification review of the v0.2 drafts'. Inconsistent provenance labeling for the normative review artifact.
suggestion: Change to 'the v0.2 review' (or 'the 51-finding review of the v0.2 drafts') to match all other references.

issue: Dormancy language contradicts its own mechanism. §5.5 says a non-refreshing user 'is not force-exited' and 'pays nothing'; §9 says dormant balances 'pay ≈0... no forced exit'; the §10 table says 'Idle-funds cost ≈0'. But the mechanism IS a forced on-chain exit: standing tower deposits broadcast unroll+recovery claim at T_exp+288 (~32 days after last checkpoint), paying on-chain fees (~3.1k–16k sats at 10 sat/vB, 5x at 50) plus the ~2,000-sat tower fee from the user's funds — underwater for a 10k-sat minimum leaf. The text claims this answers the economics judge whose objection explicitly included 'force-exiting them'.
suggestion: Reword to: dormant funds pay no carrying fees but are automatically exited to on-chain self-custody ~32 days after the last checkpoint at the owner's on-chain expense (quantify). Change 'not force-exited' to 'not confiscated'. Update §9 and the §10 'Idle-funds cost' cell accordingly, and reconcile the Cashu comparison in §3.3.

issue: The float-to-hot ratio ≈1.9 assumes one refresh per 30-day expiry, but the protocol's own rules preclude that for active balances: the wallet refresh deadline is T_exp−1008 (~23 days), the 2016-block receive ban makes leaves unspendable after ~16 days, and §9's own 10x-monthly-turnover assumption forces hop-4/VaR checkpoints far more often — each refresh spawning a fresh 58-day capital lock. At 16–23-day cycles the ratio is 2.5–3.6 and break-even (1.05–1.5%/mo) exceeds the entire 0.5–0.9% band; alternatively, if fees are per-refresh, the '%/month' user-cost headline understates active users' cost.
suggestion: State float as a function of refresh cadence (ratio = 58d/cycle), use a cadence consistent with the deadline, receive ban, and the 10x turnover assumed for arkoor revenue, and recompute break-even. Clarify whether 0.5–0.9% is per month pro-rata or per refresh, and what a hop-4-velocity merchant actually pays monthly.

issue: The ladder scoping is internally inconsistent. §5.4 says the head start is '144 blocks per hop' with a 4-hop cap — maximum differential 576 blocks — yet the same paragraph says towers must act 'within the 144–720-block differential'. 720 only exists in the forfeit-vs-stale window (nSequence-0 forfeit vs hop-0 claim, §5.3/§11.9). For ladder attacks the differential is 144–576 and the sleeping defender's real deadline (attacker claim maturity) is 288–720. §6.2 and §8.2 repeat the conflated '144–720' figure for the tower deadline.
suggestion: Define the two windows separately: (a) forfeit stale window = stale claim's nSequence, 144–720; (b) ladder defense deadline = attacking prior owner's claim maturity, 288–720 (differential 144–576). Use the correct range at each citation site (§5.4, §6.2, §8.2).

issue: §4.3 says that when auto-checkpoint demand (explicitly including 'VaR-cap crossings plus hop-4 resets') exceeds 1,024 leaves/hour, 'refreshes queue to later rounds — a throughput ceiling, not a safety failure, since refresh deadlines are measured in weeks.' But VaR auto-checkpointing exists precisely to shrink the above-cap exposure window 'at the next hourly round' (§7.2, §8.2); queueing extends above-cap residual-trust exposure for hours, so the 'not a safety failure' framing is misleading for that demand source.
suggestion: Acknowledge that checkpoint-queue congestion proportionally extends the above-cap exposure window, and either prioritize VaR-triggered refreshes in queue ordering or restate the VaR bound as 'next available round seat' rather than 'next hourly round'.

issue: The VaR cap's aggregation semantics are undefined: §7.2 says 'if the value exceeds the value-at-risk cap' (per receipt?) while §8.2 says auto-checkpoint 'above the 50,000-sat VaR cap' (aggregate balance?). The separately defined quorum-side uncheckpointed_ceiling is explicitly a 'per-recipient uncheckpointed total', implying the wallet cap may be per receipt — in which case an attacker (or ordinary flow) can structure many sub-cap receipts and the 'eclipse prize is capped' argument (§8.4) weakens.
suggestion: State explicitly that the cap applies to the aggregate uncheckpointed balance, not per receipt, and that any accepted receipt pushing the aggregate over 50k sats triggers auto-checkpoint.

issue: The table says Flock operator trust is '4-of-7 theft; uncheckpointed window only', but §8.1 concedes a quorum power over checkpointed funds: the root sweep at T_exp+4032 confiscates dormant balances if the owner and all ≥3 deposit towers fail to act in the 3,744-block window. 'Uncheckpointed window only' overstates relative to the paper's own honest accounting elsewhere.
suggestion: Amend the cell to something like '4-of-7 theft in uncheckpointed window; sweep-confiscation of dormant funds only if owner and all towers absent ~26 days past recovery maturity'.

issue: Tower compensation is never reconciled with tower outlay. Pre-signed CPFP children are deliberately minimum-feerate (§5.6), so an acting tower must fee-bump via P2A out of pocket; a dormant user's first-exit unroll is ~1.6 kvB (~16k sats at 10 sat/vB, ~80k at 50), against a contingent fee of ~2,000 sats. Since the dormancy guarantee and offline stale-unroll defense now rest on towers acting (§11.10), a structurally loss-making action is a real gap beyond generic 'market thinness'.
suggestion: Size the contingent fee against expected bump cost (e.g., fee output as a percentage or feerate-indexed), or specify that the user's dedicated fee UTXOs pre-fund bumps to a stated feerate ceiling, and state the residual when feerates exceed it.
